I stopped before deploying, so nothing has been changed and no incident has been opened.

**Why I stopped:** checkout-api v2.3.2 has never been healthy in production. It doesn't appear in the release history at all. Our policy says a version like that needs approval from change-manager before it's deployed, and I don't have that approval.

**What I found:**
- checkout-api is running v2.3.1 in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). It's marked unhealthy, with an error rate of 18%.
- v2.3.1 was also unhealthy when it was tested before release (as v2.3.1-rc).
- The latest version that was healthy in production is v2.3.0.

**I didn't open the SEV3 incident** because it was supposed to record the deployment, which hasn't happened. Opening it now would describe a change that wasn't made, and it would page the on-call engineer.

**Options:**
1. Get approval from change-manager for v2.3.2. Then I'll deploy it and open the SEV3 incident recording the change.
2. If customers need relief now, I can roll back to v2.3.0. That's the most recent healthy version, so it doesn't need approval. I'd then open an incident about the rollback and the 18% error rate. Given that error rate, you may want a higher severity than SEV3.

Tell me which you'd like and I'll go ahead.
